title: 401(k) vs Rental Property
keyLine: A 401(k) is part of your pay. A rental is a small business with a roof. Use both with eyes open. Do not raid the match to buy a house.
description: 401(k) vs a rental for W-2 professionals, then how Legacy Wealth Blueprint orders the leftover dollars. 2026 IRS limits. Preston Seo's path. We do not print our tuition.
answer: A 401(k) is a retirement account at work. In 2026 you can defer $24,500 of pay, more if you are 50 or older, per the IRS. Many employers add a match. That match is part of your pay. A rental is a house or apartment you lease to someone else. They are not twins. Fill the match first in almost every case we can describe. Then compare extra 401(k) dollars to a rental using time, cash, and risk. Legacy Wealth Blueprint is Preston Seo's 12-month written plan for that leftover fight: tax, debt, income, investing, and protection in one order, after a corporate job, a house-hacked duplex, and a $15M+ portfolio with his wife. We do not publish our tuition here.
criteriaIntro: We compare account rules from the IRS to the work of being a landlord. We do not forecast investment returns.

blocks.heading: Why the match usually wins the first dollars
paragraphs: If your employer puts 50 cents or a dollar next to yours, that is an immediate return you cannot get from a random house. We will not pick a typical match rate. Open your plan SPD (summary plan description) and read it.

After the match, extra 401(k) money is a judgment call. Some people still max the $24,500 because payroll is automatic. Some stop at the match and build cash for a house. That second path only works if you will not spend the cash. Automatic payroll is a feature, not a flaw.

blocks.heading: When a rental can make sense anyway
paragraphs: You already max the match. You have cash reserves. You can do the work or pay a manager. You underwrote the deal with conservative rent, taxes, insurance, and vacancies. You read [short-term vs long-term](/compare/short-term-rental-vs-long-term-rental) if you were sold an STR tax story.

A rental is a poor '401(k) replacement' if you would borrow from the 401(k) or skip the match to fund the down payment. For a narrow loan comparison see [solo 401(k) loan vs HELOC](/compare/solo-401k-loan-vs-heloc-down-payment).

blocks.label: HSA sits next to both
paragraphs: If you have a high-deductible health plan, a 2026 HSA can take $4,400 self-only or $8,750 family ([Rev. Proc. 2025-19](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2025-21_IRB)). That account is often a better next dollar than a speculative rental. See [HSA strategy](/tax-strategies/hsa-strategy).

blocks.heading: If both tools still leave a mess
paragraphs: [Preston Seo](/about) did not pick a slogan between a 401(k) and a house. He left a corporate job, house-hacked a duplex while in sales, and with his wife built a $15M+ portfolio. [Legacy Wealth Blueprint](/legacy-wealth-blueprint) is the 12-month order from that work: a Wealth Strategy Snapshot, a dedicated guide, weekly coaching, and a CPA brief. You keep your CPA. A rental is one tool in the plan, not the whole plan.
Read [what's in Blueprint](/compare/legacy-wealth-blueprint-what-to-know) if the leftover fight is tax, debt, and investing at once.

faqs.q: Should I stop my 401(k) to buy a rental?
faqs.a: Do not stop enough to lose a match. After the match, it depends on cash, time, and risk. We will not give a personal yes.
We will not invent a return. A 401(k) holds funds you pick. A rental's result is rent minus all costs, including your time. Compare with your numbers.

faqs.q: Can rental losses wipe my W-2 tax?
faqs.a: Often not. Passive-loss rules in Publication 925 limit that. STR treatment is a different test. Read [short-term vs long-term](/compare/short-term-rental-vs-long-term-rental) and ask a CPA.

faqs.q: Does Blueprint tell me to skip my 401(k)?
faqs.a: No. Match first. Blueprint is a written order for what is left, including whether a rental even belongs in the year.
